title: 360 ONE WAM LTD - 542772 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: 360 ONE Q1 FY27: total revenue up 20% to Rs 870 crore, PAT up 14.8% to Rs 330 crore, cost-to-income 51.3%.
summary.overview: Total ARR AUM rose 19% to Rs 3.42 lakh crore and ARR net flows were Rs 10,815 crore, up from Rs 8,985 crore in Q4, led by wealth flows of Rs 13,379 crore. ARR revenue grew 20.3% YoY to Rs 614 crore (75% of revenue) and TBR rose 37.3% to Rs 208 crore. Asset management net flows were negative because of one large institutional redemption despite gross flows of about Rs 4,000 crore. Management guided cost-to-income down 100-150 bp for FY27 and ARR retention to stay in a 70-75 bp band.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 614 crore (75% of revenue from operations)

financial_highlights.change: down from about 78 bp per management

segments.name: Wealth management
segments.commentary: Wealth net flows Rs 13,379 crore vs Rs 6,957 crore in Q4; wealth AUM Rs 2.42 lakh crore (+24.2%). UHNI franchise is the anchor; HNI program has 60+ RMs, 12 locations, over Rs 5,000 crore AUM for 800+ clients.

segments.name: Asset management
segments.commentary: AUM crossed Rs 1 lakh crore (+8.2%). Gross flows about Rs 4,000 crore but net flows negative from one large institutional mandate partial redemption. Listed strategies are about 8-9% of revenue.

segments.name: Institutional equity / B&K
segments.commentary: Covers 550+ mid and small-cap companies and 300+ institutional clients; over 85% of broking revenue from cash. Listed equity brokerage run-rate about Rs 310-320 crore annualised per management, versus Rs 250-260 crore at acquisition.

segments.name: ET Money
segments.commentary: Run-rate quarterly loss excluding exit costs cut to about Rs 3-4 crore from Rs 7 crore last quarter; management expects break-even by end of Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Cost-to-income expected to fall about 100-150 bp for FY27, with Q4 FY27 around 49-49.5% from 51%.
HNI business expected to break even on direct cost by year-end and possibly turn slightly profitable this year.
ARR retention expected to stay in a 70-75 bp range, with carry-driven quarters at the high end of the range.
Carry (AIF) guided at about 3-5 bp of alternates AUM, roughly Rs 240 crore for the year on Rs 60,000 crore base.
TBR guided to Rs 125-160 crore a quarter, growing organically 15-20% a year.
UBS collaboration: target $500-600 million of AUM exchanged between the two firms over time; first fund launches expected in the coming quarter.
capex_capacity: Net new RM target: 350-400 senior RMs and 9,000-10,000 families over three years versus 4,100 families today; implies about 30-40 RM additions a year.
ESOP scheme of about 12 lakh SARs, approximately Rs 60 crore cost spread over 4 years, starting next quarter once approved and allotted.
HNI platform: AUM moved from about Rs 4,000 crore to Rs 5,100-5,200 crore; plan to migrate about 4,000 clients of Rs 1-10 crore (Rs 17,000-18,000 crore AUM) to the HNI team over about three months.
ECM team: about 6 people hired; management expects full-strength team by October-December and active pitching from January 2027.
demand_pricing: UHNI clients above Rs 10 crore rose to above 4,000 from about 1,800-2,000 about 36 months ago.
Retention by product: advisory about 30-35 bp, large advisory mandates 25-27 bp, discretionary 40-45 bp, distribution 65-70 bp; HNI distribution about 85-90 bp; UHNI distribution 71-73 bp.
Retention decline from about 78 bp to 73-74 bp attributed about 2-2.5 bp to carry recognition and about 2 bp to business mix (advisory versus distribution, and seasonally lower TBR in Q1-Q2).
PMS structurally challenged; management expects new flows to go into AIF, MF or SIF wrappers instead.
Private credit: 360 ONE operates mainly in 10-11% and 13-15% yield buckets, not deep private credit; no semi-liquid funds in India per management.
Management expects net flows split about 70:30 or 75:25 in favour of wealth, with asset management flows averaged out by product launches over six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Will net flows tilt towards wealth given PMS outflows, and what is the outlook on the 12-15% net flow target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management still expects a 70:30 to 75:25 wealth-to-AM split; one institutional mandate cut its allocation from about $550-600 million to $175-180 million. PMS is being replaced by AIF, MF and SIF structures.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost-to-income keep declining through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: ET Money loss reduction and HNI scaling should cut 100-150 bp; Q4 target 49-49.5%. UHNI long-term cost-to-income seen at 44-47%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retention decline and how should it be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention fell from about 78 bp to 73-74 bp, mostly carry recognition and mix. Management expects a 70-75 bp range going forward, with listed AM the only structural pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics of UBS flows and effect on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UBS flows are accretive without disproportionate cost; exact retention and unit economics to be seen over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the TBR and transaction pipeline include large deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Lumpy transactions are declining as co-investment vehicles convert deals into ARR. Listed equity brokerage of about Rs 75 crore a quarter is seen as the stable base; TBR target Rs 125-160 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 12-13 crore exceptional cost and the new ESOP cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 12-13 crore is ESOP cost linked to the B&K acquisition. The new 12 lakh SAR grant adds about Rs 60 crore over four years from next quarter.

risks_watch: Institutional mandate redemptions and weak FII and global allocation to listed equity could keep AM net flows volatile.
Retention pressure from listed AM (8-9% of revenue) and mix shift towards advisory.
Cost-to-income depends on ET Money break-even by Q4 FY27 and HNI migration of about 4,000 clients; new ESOPs add cost from next quarter.
ECM build-out is at an early stage and ECM contributes under Rs 8 crore a quarter; management targets 15-20% of a Rs 750-1,000 crore TBR base in 2-3 years.
UBS collaboration economics not yet disclosed; first fund launches expected next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, flows and the cost-to-income path, with specific numeric targets. More cautious and vague on UBS unit economics, the PMS outflow structure and ECM timing, and deflected the CEO succession question by stating his own commitment.
key_quotes: We are very happy to report a profit after tax of Rs 330 crores an increase of 14.8%.
I think the private credit industry is in a very, very nascent stage in our country.
So, in some senses, it's a perpetual hiring curve.

adds.what: Net new RM target of 350-400 senior RMs and 9,000-10,000 families over three years (vs 4,100 families today)
HNI platform AUM expansion to Rs 5,100-5,200 crore with migration of ~4,000 clients (Rs 17,000-18,000 crore AUM) over about three months

growth.why: Q1 FY27 total revenue grew 20% YoY to Rs 870 crore and management guided cost-to-income down 100-150 bp in FY27 (Q4 FY27 about 49-49.5%), backed by wealth flows of Rs 13,379 crore and a 350-400 RM hiring plan over three years, though no explicit revenue growth % was guided and capacity additions are people/platform rather than hard capacity.
